title: Stalled 1 to 3 s: the puck
note: A blip. From 1 s of a stall a 56 dp spinner puck at the card's anchor (bottom centre), instead of PlayerView's spinner in the middle of the picture. Gone the moment it plays.

title: Stalled 3 s: checking
note: At 3 s the puck opens into the card and the checks run (about 2 s). Each link fills with the pink progress as its answer comes back, left to right.

title: Cause: the provider is slow
note: The owner's question answered: not you, them. The two numbers side by side are the evidence. OK switches to the game's other feed (its own score delay; never automatic). No score anywhere.

title: Cause: weak Wi-Fi
note: Wi-Fi 1 of 4 bars and the stream starving: the link from the TV to the router is the problem. OK steps down to the stream's 720p level (needs 5 Mbps).

title: Cause: slow internet
note: On a network cable, so it isn't Wi-Fi; a 3 s speed sample says the line itself is short. OK plays the provider's HD copy of the channel (needs 9 Mbps).

title: Cause: the TV is offline
note: Android says there is no network: shown at once (no 3 s wait, no checks). It tunes again the moment the network is back. OK opens the TV's network settings.

title: Cause: the provider isn't answering
note: Google answers, the provider doesn't: it's them, and nothing on this TV can fix it. airglow keeps reconnecting by itself (1, 2, 4… s); the countdown says when.

title: Cause: every stream is in use
note: A 403 or 401 with the provider's own count full (active_cons = max_connections). The same card as catch-up's player-connlimit, with the path added.

title: Keeps pausing: the chip
note: Short pauses that each got under 3 s, but the third in 5 minutes: the action chip's slot and timing (10 s, any key dismisses), the cause in one line, the action on OK.

title: A movie: slow internet
note: Movies and episodes get the same card; the last node reads Movie. A film can wait, so the best action is to pause and fill the buffer (the card then counts what's loaded); the 1080p copy is in Details.

title: Stopped: the channel is off
note: A 404 twice in a row while the provider's own server answers: the channel is down at their end. Replaces "This channel stopped · The provider may be down".

title: Stopped: a game feed is off
note: A game channel: the other feeds first, as today, one OK away; each keeps its own score delay. No score or clock on the card.

title: Stopped: the TV can't decode it
note: A decoder error: the only cause on the TV itself, said plainly so nobody restarts the router. The provider's other copy first.

title: Options: the Connection row
note: ◀ in the player. Connection sits under Quality; its value is the live verdict (Good, Slow, Weak Wi-Fi, Offline, Checking…) and its line the one number that matters.

title: The Connection panel: all good
note: Options > Connection: the same five links, upright, each with its reading. Opening it runs the quick checks (under 2 s); the speed test only on Check again.

title: The Connection panel: during the stall
note: Hold OK on the card (or Options > Connection) during the stall: every reading, then every action in order, the best one focused. No score; the game is named only by its feed.

title: Account: Check the connection
note: Account > Provider gets one row under Check the guide. The same test as the player's panel, from the sofa, without a channel stalling.

title: The check, running
note: OK on the row: the five links checked in order, about 10 s in all. Nothing to press while it runs; Back stops it.

title: The check: all good
note: The result in one line, in what it means for him (4K, HD), over the readings. The last channel is sampled for 5 s only if a stream is free.

title: The check: Wi-Fi is the weak link
note: A finding: the speed is only as good as the Wi-Fi gives it. The advice is the one thing that fixes it for good, in plain words.
